note: Events for the player's party; AI parties meet the same list and choose for themselves. Effects: op is money | rep | heat | volunteers | awareness | buzz | donors | sigs | recognition; scope is 'home' (default) or 'state'. Conditions in 'when': minDay (days since founding), minHeat, minMoney, needsOffice, qualified, minSeats. Nothing here refers to a real person, party position or real election.

events.title: The diner debate
events.text: A regular at the busiest diner in town challenges your leader to defend the platform, loudly, in front of the breakfast crowd.

choices.label: Take the challenge
choices.result: It goes well enough. People are talking.

choices.label: Buy the room coffee and listen
choices.result: A few of them sign up to help.

events.title: A call from the local paper
events.text: The editor wants an interview about why anyone would start a new party here. The piece could run long.

choices.label: Give a careful, honest interview
choices.result: A fair write-up on page three.

choices.label: Go on the attack against both big parties
choices.result: Front page. Not everyone liked it.

events.title: Burnout
events.text: Your most reliable volunteers have been out every weekend for months. Two of them are talking about quitting.

choices.label: Throw them a proper thank-you dinner

events.title: The hardware store owner
events.text: A well-liked shop owner offers a donation and a window sign, and hints that she would like a say in your platform.

choices.label: Welcome her as a founding donor
Decline politely
choices.result: Word gets round that you cannot be bought.

events.title: County fair season
events.text: A booth at the county fair costs money and three days of volunteer time, and half the county walks past it.

events.title: Signatures challenged
events.text: A lawyer files a challenge to a batch of your petition signatures, claiming bad addresses.

choices.label: Hire counsel and defend every line
Let the batch go and collect more
Have a friend at the board make the challenge disappear
choices.result: The challenge is withdrawn. Someone will remember why.

events.title: A name on the ballot
events.text: Your party's line will appear on the ballot. Reporters who ignored you for years are suddenly calling.

choices.label: Hold a press conference on the statehouse steps
Celebrate at home with the people who did the work

events.title: A defector
events.text: A fictional county chair from one of the established parties is fed up and wants to cross over, bringing a mailing list.

choices.label: Welcome them publicly
choices.result: A splash, and some grumbling from your old hands.

events.title: The big cheque
events.text: A wealthy developer will fund a full year of operations. He expects his calls returned.

choices.label: Take it, with a public disclosure
choices.result: The money is real. So is the headline.

choices.label: Take it through a shell committee
Turn it down
choices.result: Small donors hear about it and chip in.

events.title: After the storm
events.text: A bad storm has left part of the county without power. Your volunteers could knock on doors with water and blankets instead of leaflets.

choices.label: Send everyone out to help
choices.result: People will remember who showed up.

events.title: Left off the stage
events.text: The organisers of a candidate forum have invited only the two established parties.

choices.label: Hold your own forum the same night
choices.result: A smaller room, a warmer crowd.

events.title: A bad post
events.text: A volunteer posted something crude from the party's account at two in the morning.

choices.label: Say nothing and hope
choices.result: It does not pass in a day.

events.title: An evening at the union hall
events.text: A local is willing to hear you out. They have been let down before.

choices.label: Go, listen, promise only what the platform says
choices.result: Respectful applause. A few cards filled in.

events.title: Lunch with the chamber of commerce
events.text: The chamber wants to know whether your party is good for business. Lunch is on them.

choices.label: Go, listen, promise only what the platform says

events.title: Campaign finance audit
events.text: The state elections office has selected your committee for a routine audit.

choices.label: Open the books fully
choices.result: They find sloppiness, and note your cooperation.

choices.label: Tidy the records first
choices.result: The audit closes. The tidying is its own risk.

events.title: Ribbon cutting
events.text: As an office-holder, your leader is asked to open a new community centre built with money they voted for.

events.title: A hard vote
events.text: A budget vote pits what your platform says against what a noisy room of constituents wants tonight.

events.title: A favour asked
events.text: A contractor would be grateful, in cash, if a permit moved faster. Your leader's office could make that happen.

choices.label: Report the offer
choices.result: A small story, a clean name.

events.title: Students want in
events.text: A group at the community college wants to start a campus chapter.

choices.label: Give them a logo and good wishes

events.title: A whisper campaign
events.text: Someone is spreading a false story about your leader. You could answer it, or offer to trade one of your own.

choices.label: Pay a blogger to muddy the water
choices.result: Everybody looks worse. You look a little less worse.

events.title: A statewide profile
events.text: A public radio programme wants to spend a day with the party that keeps winning seats.

choices.label: Open the doors
choices.result: A long, fair segment heard across the state.

events.title: Coffee with a rival
events.text: An organiser from another small party suggests sharing volunteer lists for a season.

choices.label: Share lists
choices.result: More doors knocked on both sides.

events.title: A bequest
events.text: A retired schoolteacher who never missed a meeting has left the party a modest sum in her will.

choices.label: Name a volunteer award after her

events.title: Late paperwork
events.text: The quarterly finance report went in four days late. The fine is automatic.

choices.label: Backdate the filing
choices.result: No fine. A small lie on a public record.
